bio: University of Amsterdam & VU Amsterdam cognitive neuroscientists and researchers.

I am a cognitive neuroscientist working at the Brain and Cognition group (Department of Psychology) of the University of Amsterdam. In our lab we study the neural correlates of consciousness and the role of consciousness in cognitive control and decision-making using various neuroimaging techniques (e.g., high-density EEG, functional and structural MRI, MEG).

bio: I am a cognitive neuroscientist in the Cognitive Psychology department at VU Amsterdam and the Brain and Cognition group at UvA. In the Conscious Brain Lab we use EEG, fMRI and psychophysics to investigate consciousness, perceptual bias, confidence, and automatic sensory control. I developed the open-source ADAM toolbox for multivariate EEG/MEG decoding.

name: Ivan Ivanchei
bio: I joined the Conscious Brain Lab in August 2024 with a Marie Curie project on probabilistic learning and awareness. My research investigates how people become aware of what they learn in probabilistic environments, using behavioral, metacognitive, and physiological indices.

name: Maartje de Jong
bio: I investigate how the brain transforms sensory input into meaningful visual perception, using MRI, scalp and intracranial EEG, and psychophysics. My research examines phenomena such as optical illusions, perceptual learning, ambiguous images, binocular rivalry, and face perception.

name: Ana-Maria Barosan
bio: I started my PhD at the Conscious Brain Lab in September 2024, supervised by Simon van Gaal and Timo Stein. I investigate how arousal shapes perceptual decision-making using fMRI, EEG, psychophysics, pupillometry, and pharmacological methods.

name: Margot Steijger
bio: I joined the Conscious Brain Lab as a PhD candidate, supported by an ERC Consolidator Grant. My research investigates how arousal shapes performance and conscious perception, using behavioural, pupillometric, neural, and physiological measures.

name: Sean van Mil
bio: I am a PhD candidate in the Conscious Brain Lab, supervised by Simon van Gaal and supported by an ERC Consolidator Grant. Building on research at the University of Cambridge, I investigate how arousal shapes decision-making, performance, and conscious perception.
